description:
NOT a v1 goal — activated when the French market is prioritized. The ADR-003 audit trail is designed so this epic is purely additive: period closures (Z/daily/monthly/fiscal-year), fiscal archives, audit export in an auditor-consumable format, across all cash paths (web, POS, cashless). First task when picked up: verify the inferred ISCA reading (inalterability, security, conservation, archiving — art. 286-I-3° bis CGI / NF525 referential) against the referential's actual text.

**Conditions of Success:**
- Closures compute and seal period totals; sealed periods are provably inalterable
- Fiscal archive export in an auditor-consumable format
- Profile lands with zero schema/flow changes to the ADR-003 journal — this validates the ADR's core claim
- Requirements traceable to the NF525 referential text; gaps explicitly listed

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map) · docs/adr/ADR-003-append-only-audit-trail.md

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

Scope amended pre-Gate-1 (owner directive 2026-07-12): NF525 is NOT an immediate goal — it becomes a later-phase French-market profile. The underlying requirement is generalized: traceability is a must, with the same audit-trail thinking for money AND tickets (ADR-003 reworked accordingly).

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Scope grew — from the TKT-57 retro (R6). Read before planning this ticket.**

[ADR-021](../../docs/adr/ADR-021-ticket-lifecycle-trail-integrity.md) (TKT-57) makes TKT-11 the owner of something it did not previously own: **the attacker-independent trust domain the ticket lifecycle trail depends on.** This is no longer only a fiscal-archive ticket, and sizing it as one will under-scope it.

ADR-021 §The trust boundary establishes that *state inside the Access database cannot constrain an adversary who writes to that database*. Four separate mechanisms therefore park here until TKT-11 provides an outside:

1. **Targeted rollback detection** — a per-ticket chain plus checkpoint truncation verifies clean. Only an external attestation over checkpoint roots detects it. The delta-checkpoint structure exists specifically so this costs one attestation per interval instead of one per ticket head.
2. **Signer continuity** — the checkpoint signer must refuse to extend a chain whose head regressed, which requires a last-observed root held where the DB adversary cannot reach it.
3. **Quarantine + threshold integrity** (ADR-021 §Decision 6) — currently rows in Access, so they bound our own bugs, not attackers.
4. **Epoch-signature completeness** (§Decision 5) — a retained epoch signature is deletable; containing a current-key compromise needs an externally retained rotation manifest.

Also inherited: ADR-021 §Decision 3 fixes the checkpoint interval (60s default) as a **permanent** bound on what any anchor can ever attest — a head rolled back before its first checkpoint was never committed to anything, and shortening the interval later does not backfill coverage.

ADR-016 §D7 already named TKT-11 as the owner of the money journal's rollback deferral. TKT-57 adds the ticket trail to that list. Sequencing note: TKT-67 implements ADR-021 and can ship without this, but until it lands the trail is tamper-evident against modification and insertion only.
